record.field: The legacy authentication server (auth-legacy-01) still requires TLS 1.0 for backward compatibility with older client applications. TLS 1.0 has known vulnerabilities and should be disabled, but cannot be removed until all clients are migrated to TLS 1.2+.
Potential man-in-the-middle attacks on legacy authentication traffic. Affects approximately 15% of client connections.
TLS 1.0 is vulnerable to BEAST and POODLE attacks. While compensating controls reduce exposure, the risk remains elevated until full migration.
Critical business applications depend on legacy clients that only support TLS 1.0. Immediate removal would disrupt operations for approximately 200 users.
Client migration requires firmware updates that are scheduled over the next 90 days. A parallel TLS 1.2 endpoint has been deployed for migrated clients.
Legacy authentication server isolated to a dedicated VLAN with restricted access from only known client subnets.
IDS rules configured to detect anomalous TLS 1.0 handshake patterns and alert the SOC.

Production database server (db-prod-03) cannot be patched for CVE-2025-XXXX due to vendor certification requirements. The patch requires a major version upgrade which must be validated by the application vendor before deployment.
Remote code execution vulnerability. If exploited, could lead to full database compromise including customer PII.
CVSS 9.8 vulnerability with known exploit code available. Database contains sensitive financial and personal data.
Vendor certification process requires 45 days. Applying the patch without certification would void the support contract and potentially destabilize the production environment.
The patch requires PostgreSQL major version upgrade (14 → 16). Application compatibility testing is underway but not yet complete.
Database access restricted to application servers only. All direct connections blocked at the firewall level.
All database queries logged and forwarded to SIEM for real-time analysis and anomaly detection.
Shared Service Account — Legacy Batch Processing

The nightly batch processing system uses a shared service account (svc_batch_legacy) rather than individual service accounts per application. This violates the principle of least privilege and makes audit attribution difficult.
Compromised shared account would grant access to multiple batch systems. Audit logs cannot distinguish between applications using the same account.
Migrating to individual service accounts requires reconfiguration of 12 batch jobs across 4 departments. The migration is planned but resource-constrained.

During the 3rd floor renovation, employees required temporary access to the guest WiFi network for workstations that could not be connected to the wired network. The guest network has reduced security controls compared to the corporate network.
Employees on guest network bypass network-level DLP and advanced threat protection. Limited to 3rd floor personnel during renovation.
Office renovation required disconnecting wired network drops. Employees needed connectivity to continue working.
VPN enforcement was enabled on all affected workstations to tunnel traffic through the corporate network despite using guest WiFi.
Renovation complete. All workstations reconnected to corporate wired network. Guest WiFi access removed. Verified via network scan — no remaining corporate devices on guest VLAN.
All workstations configured with always-on VPN when connected to guest WiFi, ensuring traffic is routed through corporate security controls.

Manufacturing floor control systems run Windows Server 2012 R2, which is no longer receiving security updates. Upgrading requires vendor recertification of the SCADA/HMI software, which is currently scheduled for Q3.
Unpatched OS vulnerable to multiple known exploits. Manufacturing systems contain proprietary process data and control critical production equipment.
Multiple CVEs affecting Windows Server 2012 R2 remain unpatched. System is air-gapped but accessible via jump server for maintenance.
SCADA vendor requires recertification before OS upgrade. Unplanned upgrade could void manufacturing warranty and halt production.
OS upgrade requires SCADA software v7.x which is currently in vendor testing. ETA for certified release is 60 days.
Manufacturing systems physically isolated from corporate network. Access only via dedicated jump server with MFA.
Weekly review of jump server access logs and manufacturing system event logs for indicators of compromise.
